unit.tutorContext: Module 5 teaches the hair follicle and the melanocortin system in four separate registers (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). Follicle: ex vivo human scalp follicles run an HPA-like loop (CRH → POMC products → cortisol, with feedback) and a GH/IGF-1-like loop (D, organ culture, Paus group); local DHT miniaturises susceptible follicles (androgenetic alopecia); anagen immune-privilege collapse underlies alopecia areata. Baricitinib: BRAVE-AA1/AA2, 1,200 adults, SALT ≤20 at week 36 in up to 39% on baricitinib vs 3–6% on placebo; FDA-approved 13 Jun 2022 for adults with severe alopecia areata (A). A&RE hair-loss workup: patterned → AGA (topical minoxidil; finasteride in men); diffuse after trigger → telogen effluvium (reassure, ferritin, TSH); patchy smooth ± nail pitting → alopecia areata (dermatology referral, thyroid/autoimmune screen); androgen excess → work-up; ferritin + TSH always; scarring → biopsy; refer severe or rapid AA promptly. Minoxidil (men and women) and finasteride (men): A by RCT meta-analysis (Adil 2017); US: topical minoxidil OTC (approved 1988), finasteride Rx (1997). Melanocortins: skin makes POMC → ACTH, α-MSH, β-endorphin; MC1R pigment, MC2R adrenal, MC3R/MC4R brain (appetite; central sexual effects), MC5R sebum. Afamelanotide: MC1R agonist; two sponsor-funded phase 3 RCTs in EPP (US median 69.4 vs 40.8 pain-free sunlight hours; EU 6.0 vs 0.8); EU authorised 22 Dec 2014 (exceptional circumstances), US 2019; EPP only, manufacturer's implant; US label (Aug 2024) recommends full-body skin examination twice yearly; A for EPP; vitiligo phase 3 has no posted results. Melanotan II: non-selective MC1R/3R/4R/5R agonist, brain-penetrant; only controlled data a 3-man 1996 pilot and a 10-man 1998 ED crossover; guides disagree (Pocket Guide C, A&RE D) — course grades cosmetic use D; case-report harms: darkening/growing and eruptive atypical naevi, melanonychia, ≥5 melanomas all with other risk factors (causation unproven), ischaemic priapism, sympathomimetic toxicity with rhabdomyolysis, PRES; online vials held 43–88% of the label with impurities. Status: approved for no indication; US FDA compounding page (22 Apr 2026) lists it among withdrawn category-2 nominations with safety risks; UK MHRA (17 Apr 2024) injectables are unauthorised medicines, stop immediately; Australia TGA (17 Aug 2026) prescription-only, no ARTG product, not approved for tanning. A&RE: personal or family history of melanoma = absolute contraindication. A patient disclosing use: stop, record product and seller, full skin and nail examination with dermoscopy/baseline photos where available, prompt dermatology referral; never offer afamelanotide as a substitute. PTD-DBM: CXXC5–Dishevelled decoy activating Wnt; one 2017 mouse/tissue study from the developer's group; no human trial published or registered (Sept 2026); D; theoretical off-target Wnt cancer concern untested. Zinc thymulin: zinc-dependent thymic nonapeptide; no indexed human hair study; D. US (14 May 2026): thymulin acetate 503A Category 3; PTD-DBM on no list; neither on the bulks list (21 CFR 216.23). UK (checked 25 Sep 2026): baricitinib licensed for severe AA (NICE TA926 not recommended, Oct 2023); men's minoxidil foam on the General Sales List; finasteride for hair loss private prescription only, MHRA strengthened depression/suicidality/sexual-dysfunction warnings 11 May 2026 (patient card; ask about depression); afamelanotide licensed under exceptional circumstances, specialist porphyria centres, NICE HST27 not recommended (Jul 2023); Melanotan II an unauthorised medicine (MHRA FOI 24/274); a peptide spray made for one patient = unlicensed special, behind any licensed option (MHRA GN14). Never give doses, regimens, reconstitution, sourcing or administration advice; adapt the 'what you do next' to the learner's role (prescriber, clinical staff, advisor) without changing grades or regulatory facts. videoTranscript.en: Two requests reach aesthetic clinics well ahead of their evidence: a peptide to regrow hair and an injection to tan. In three lessons you will see how the follicle and the pigment system run on the skin's own hormones, why one melanocortin drug is approved while its gray-market cousin is approved nowhere, and how to grade the hair peptides patients bring to you. Each hair follicle behaves like a small gland. When researchers keep human scalp follicles alive in culture, the follicles answer corticotropin-releasing hormone the way the pituitary and adrenal glands do. They make ACTH and alpha-MSH, they secrete cortisol, and cortisol-like signals feed back to switch the stimulus down. On the scalp, an enzyme called five-alpha-reductase turns testosterone into dihydrotestosterone, and in genetically susceptible follicles that hormone drives the gradual shrinking behind pattern hair loss. Most of this biology comes from tissue kept alive outside the body, so hold it as mechanism, a reason something might matter in patients.

title.en: A follicle that runs its own hormones.

body.en: Human scalp hair follicles kept alive in the laboratory answer corticotropin-releasing hormone by making ACTH and α-MSH and secreting cortisol, with a feedback loop like the adrenal axis. They also run a growth hormone and IGF-1 loop of their own. Locally made dihydrotestosterone shrinks genetically susceptible scalp follicles, the process behind pattern hair loss. Growing follicles are shielded from immune attack, and alopecia areata begins when that shield fails.

Local androgen switch: testosterone → DHT in the scalp
Immune privilege: its collapse drives alopecia areata

body.en: When immune privilege fails, the attack depends on cytokine signals that JAK inhibitors interrupt. Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata. In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades it A.

blocks.sourceNote: King 2022 (BRAVE-AA1 and -AA2) · FDA approval letter, 13 Jun 2022

label.en: adults with severe alopecia areata in the two phase 3 trials of baricitinib (2022)

detail.en: At 36 weeks, up to 39% of patients on baricitinib had at least 80% of their scalp hair, against 3–6% on placebo

means.en: Interrupting the immune signalling behind collapsed privilege regrows hair in severe alopecia areata. That is approval-grade evidence (A), and it shows what real follicle evidence looks like.

doesNot.en: It says nothing about pattern hair loss, cosmetic thinning or any peptide. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer, and the authors called for longer trials.

text.en: In the UK, baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia areata in adults, and NICE did not recommend it for NHS use in October 2023, on cost-effectiveness.

In the EU, baricitinib (Olumiant) has been centrally authorised since 13 February 2017; its indications include severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over, and it is prescription-only, started by a doctor experienced in the condition (EMA). Since EMA's January 2023 review, JAK inhibitors including Olumiant should be used in people aged 65 or over, at raised cardiovascular or cancer risk, or long-term smokers only if no suitable alternative exists, and this applies to alopecia areata.
In Portugal, Olumiant (baricitinib) is classified as a restricted-prescription medicine (MSRM restrita - Alínea a), according to INFARMED's Infomed register on 25 September 2026.

In Brazil, baricitinib (Olumiant) has been registered by ANVISA since 26 November 2018, and its current label includes severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 or over weighing at least 30 kg (checked 25 September 2026).

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. The EDE register lists Olumiant (baricitinib) tablets, registered since 8 June 2017, as Prescription Only and files them under rheumatic diseases; it does not show whether alopecia areata is an approved UAE indication (25 September 2026).

audioScript.en: Most requests for a hair peptide skip the diagnosis. Start with the pattern, ask about a trigger, look for patches and nail pitting, and look for signs of androgen excess. Check ferritin and thyroid function every time, and send a scarring pattern for biopsy. The approved options already carry strong evidence. Pooled randomized trials support topical minoxidil in men and women and finasteride in men. In the United States minoxidil is sold over the counter, while finasteride for hair loss needs a prescription. Severe or fast-spreading alopecia areata belongs with a dermatologist, where a JAK inhibitor is an approved option for adults. Whatever your role, the workup comes before the product.

prescriber.en: Complete the workup and record the pattern before prescribing. Offer the approved options with their grades, refer severe or rapidly progressive alopecia areata, and document any investigational product the patient raises and what you advised. In the UK, before prescribing finasteride, ask about any history of depression, give the patient card, and review mood and sexual side effects.

clinical-staff.en: Note the pattern, the timeline and any recent trigger, photograph the scalp with consent if your setting allows, and pass it to the prescriber. Patchy or fast-spreading loss needs prompt escalation.

advisor.en: Explain what the approved options are and what their evidence shows. A patient with new, patchy, scarring or fast-spreading hair loss needs a prescriber before any product.

text.en: In the UK, topical minoxidil is licensed and a men's foam is on general sale, finasteride for hair loss is available only on private prescription, and baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia areata in adults. In May 2026 MHRA strengthened its warnings that finasteride is associated with depression, suicidal thoughts and sexual dysfunction that may persist after stopping.

In the EU, topical minoxidil is authorised nationally, finasteride tablets and a finasteride skin spray are authorised in various member states for early androgenetic alopecia in men aged 18 to 41 (EMA, 2025), and baricitinib (Olumiant) is centrally authorised and prescription-only, with severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over among its indications. After an EU-wide review endorsed on 19 June 2025, suicidal ideation is a confirmed side effect of finasteride tablets, and packs of the hair-loss tablets carry a patient card.

In Portugal, topical minoxidil is a non-prescription medicine (MNSRM), and the label of Minox 5 solution covers alopecia areata as well as androgenetic alopecia in men and women. Finasteride for hair loss (Propecia) is prescription-only (MSRM), and baricitinib (Olumiant) is a restricted-prescription medicine (MSRM restrita – point a) (INFARMED's Infomed register, 25 September 2026).

In Brazil, minoxidil products such as Aloxidil are indicated for androgenetic alopecia in adult men, and finasteride products such as Pro Hair are indicated for the treatment of men with male-pattern baldness (androgenetic alopecia). Baricitinib (Olumiant) is indicated for adult and adolescent patients aged 12 years or older and weighing at least 30 kg with severe alopecia areata (ANVISA, 25 September 2026).

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. The EDE register lists topical minoxidil (for example Regaine solution, a Pharmacist Only Medicine), oral finasteride (Propecia, Prescription Only), a topical finasteride spray registered in March 2025 (Fincrezo, Prescription Only) and Olumiant (baricitinib, Prescription Only), without showing whether alopecia areata is an approved UAE indication (25 September 2026).

title.en: Five receptors, one family of hormones.

body.en: Skin makes proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and cuts it into ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. Those peptides act on five melanocortin receptors. MC1R drives pigment in skin and hair, MC2R answers ACTH in the adrenal gland, MC3R and MC4R act in the brain on appetite, and MC5R governs sebum. Which receptors a drug reaches decides what else it does.

audioScript.en: Pigment starts with hormones the skin makes for itself. Skin cells produce a precursor called POMC and cut it into ACTH, alpha-MSH and beta-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. There are five melanocortin receptors. MC1R sets the pigment of skin and hair. MC2R is the adrenal receptor for ACTH. MC3R and MC4R work in the brain on appetite, and central receptors also drive sexual responses. MC5R governs sebum. Researchers caution that the real map is messier, with receptors turning up in more tissues than the textbook suggests. For this lesson one idea matters most. A drug that stays on MC1R mostly changes pigment, and a drug that reaches the brain's receptors brings other effects with it.

In the EU, afamelanotide (Scenesse implant) is authorised for erythropoietic protoporphyria, under exceptional circumstances (European Commission, 22 December 2014), and is prescribed only by specialists in recognised EPP centres.

In Portugal, Scenesse is authorised through the EU procedure but classified as a restricted-prescription medicine for exclusive hospital use (MSRM restrita, alínea a), and no presentation is marketed in Portugal (INFARMED's Infomed register, 25 September 2026).

In Brazil, no registered medicine containing afamelanotide (Scenesse) was found: ANVISA's open-data register and its online medicines search returned no match on 25 September 2026, and the substance is absent from ANVISA's substance dictionary.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. An ingredient and product-name search of the EDE register found no registered product containing afamelanotide, and none named Scenesse (25 September 2026).

body.en: Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain. In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, against 40.8 hours on placebo. The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer.

means.en: Afamelanotide lets people with EPP spend more time in sunlight without pain. That is approval-grade evidence (A) for one rare disease.

doesNot.en: It says nothing about cosmetic tanning, about Melanotan II, or about unsupervised injections. Even in EPP, the US label recommends a full-body skin examination twice a year.

body.en: The harms of Melanotan II come from case reports and reviews, so they show what can happen without telling you how often. Reported skin effects include darkening and growth of existing moles, crops of new and sometimes atypical naevi, and dark bands in the nails. At least five melanomas have been reported during or after use, each in someone with other risk factors, so causation is unproven. Systemic reports include ischaemic priapism needing surgery and a stimulant-like toxic reaction with rhabdomyolysis, and FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious events.

title.en: A Wnt switch and a zinc question.

body.en: PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating peptide to a short decoy sequence that stops the protein CXXC5 from binding Dishevelled. Freed from that brake, Wnt/β-catenin signalling rises, and in mice hair regrew faster. Its developers also found CXXC5 raised in human balding scalp. Zinc thymulin is a thymic peptide that is active only when bound to zinc. How it might act on hair has never been defined, and whether any effect would come from the peptide or the zinc is unknown.

Zinc thymulin: a zinc-dependent thymic peptide

body.en: A cell-penetrating tag carries a decoy sequence into follicle cells. The decoy keeps CXXC5 off Dishevelled, so Wnt signalling can rise.

A thymic hormone that works only with zinc bound. Its proposed hair effect has no defined mechanism and no indexed human study.

audioScript.en: Two peptides are sold for hair, and both arrive with better stories than data. PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating fragment borrowed from an HIV protein to a short decoy sequence. Inside follicle cells, the decoy keeps a protein called CXXC5 from binding its partner, Dishevelled, and that releases a brake on Wnt signalling, a pathway involved in hair regrowth. In mice, hair regrew faster and follicles formed in healed wounds. The work came from the developer's own group. Zinc thymulin is a thymic hormone that becomes active only when zinc binds to it. How it might help hair has never been defined, and nobody has shown whether any effect would come from the peptide or from the zinc. Hold both as mechanism, and look for the human trial.

In the EU, a medicine prepared in a pharmacy for an individual patient on prescription (a magistral formula) falls outside Directive 2001/83/EC (Article 3). A search of the Union Register and EMA's medicines data found no centrally authorised medicine containing thymulin or PTD-DBM (25 September 2026).

In Portugal, a magistral formula may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation, and the prescribing physician must satisfy themselves of its safety and efficacy (Decreto-Lei 95/2004). INFARMED's Infomed register lists no medicine containing thymulin or PTD-DBM (25 September 2026).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that a substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may only be individual, on prescription, by a pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance. A search of ANVISA's register found no registered medicine containing PTD-DBM or thymulin (25 September 2026), though immunomodulators such as thymomodulin are registered.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; under the medicines law, Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024, products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies need no marketing approval, and no product containing thymulin or PTD-DBM was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). prompt.en: Fictional case: a woman with a slowly widening central parting has been using a zinc thymulin scalp spray, and asks whether it will work.
What do you tell her first?

label.en: Name the grade plainly: D. No indexed human study has tested zinc thymulin for hair.

why.en: The useful conversation names the grade first. Zinc thymulin's proposed hair effect has no defined mechanism and no indexed human study.

label.en: Reassure her: thymulin is a natural thymic hormone, so it should help.

why.en: Being a thymic hormone says nothing about hair. How it might act on hair has never been defined, and whether any effect would come from the peptide or the zinc is unknown.

label.en: Suggest a PTD-DBM spray instead, since it releases a brake on Wnt signalling.

why.en: PTD-DBM carries grade D too: one 2017 study in mice and human scalp tissue from the developer's group, and no human trial, published or registered.

prompt.en: She asks what she should do instead. What comes next?

label.en: Go back to the diagnosis: the workup, with ferritin and TSH, comes before any product.

why.en: The conversation returns to the workup. Pattern, trigger, patches and signs of androgen excess sort most hair loss, and ferritin and TSH are checked in everyone.

label.en: Keep the spray going for a few more months, then decide.

why.en: That skips the diagnosis. Whatever your role, the workup comes before the product.

label.en: Refer her for a JAK inhibitor.

why.en: A JAK inhibitor is an approved option for adults with severe or fast-spreading alopecia areata, which shows as patchy, smooth loss. Her hair loss needs the workup first.

prompt.en: The workup points to androgenetic alopecia, and her ferritin and TSH are normal. What now?

label.en: Describe the approved options, such as topical minoxidil (A), and make sure the spray, where it came from and the grade you quoted go in her notes.

why.en: Pooled randomized trials support topical minoxidil in men and women. When a patient already uses a peptide spray, record the product, the source and the grade you quoted.

label.en: Describe topical minoxidil, and leave the spray out of her notes: it was her own choice.

why.en: The product she raised belongs in the notes: record the product, the source and the grade you quoted, and what you advised.

label.en: Arrange a scalp biopsy before any treatment.

why.en: A scarring pattern goes to biopsy. Her patterned thinning points to androgenetic alopecia, where the approved options come next.

done.en: Name the grade, go back to the diagnosis, describe the approved options, and record the product she raised.

prompt.en: Closing Module 5: which statement keeps the four registers apart for Melanotan II?

text.en: It shares afamelanotide's receptor, so it shares afamelanotide's approval.

why.en: That blends mechanism into regulatory status. The approval belongs to afamelanotide, for EPP only.

text.en: Mechanism: a non-selective melanocortin agonist. Evidence: two tiny 1990s studies and case reports of harm (D). Status: approved nowhere, with US, UK and Australian regulators on record against it. Open question: whether it causes melanoma.

why.en: Correct. Four separate answers, each with its own source.

text.en: Because melanoma causation is unproven, it is safe to use with monitoring.

why.en: An unproven cause is an open question and offers no reassurance; the documented harms and the lack of approval still stand.

feedback.en: Mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question: four answers, never one sentence.

prompt.en: Which statement about afamelanotide and Melanotan II is accurate?

text.en: Afamelanotide is approved (EU 2014, US 2019) only for erythropoietic protoporphyria; Melanotan II is approved for no indication, and regulators in the US, UK and Australia have warned about it.

why.en: Correct. Same receptor family, different molecules, and only one has an approval, for one rare disease.

text.en: Afamelanotide's US approval covers cosmetic tanning.

why.en: The US indication is to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with EPP; tanning is not an approved use.

text.en: Melanotan II became approvable once FDA reviewed it for compounding.

why.en: Its compounding nomination was withdrawn, and FDA's page lists serious safety risks. A review is never an approval.

rationale.en: Approval attaches to a specific product and indication; a shared receptor transfers neither evidence nor legal standing.

prompt.en: A patient asks about a PTD-DBM hair spray. Which grade fits its evidence, and why?

text.en: A, because it acts on the central Wnt pathway of hair growth.

why.en: A plausible pathway is mechanism, and grades rest on human evidence.

text.en: D: one 2017 study in mice and scalp tissue from the developer's group, and no human trial published or registered as of September 2026.

why.en: Correct. Animal and tissue data only, from one group with a commercial link.

text.en: C, because small human trials show regrowth.

why.en: No human trial of PTD-DBM exists, small or large.

rationale.en: Grade the human evidence, then say who produced it; a strong mechanism with no trial in people is D.

answer.en: Afamelanotide (Scenesse) is an MC1R agonist approved only for erythropoietic protoporphyria (EU 2014, US 2019; licensed in the UK, where NICE did not recommend it for NHS use in 2023), on the strength of two sponsor-funded phase 3 trials; even there, the US label recommends a full-body skin examination twice a year. Melanotan II is a different, non-selective molecule approved for no indication. Its only controlled human data are two tiny 1990s studies, and case reports describe darkening and new moles, nail pigmentation, melanomas in people with other risk factors (causation unproven), priapism and rhabdomyolysis. FDA (April 2026), MHRA (April 2024) and TGA (August 2026) have all put warnings on record. If someone has used it: stop, record the product and seller, examine the skin and nails, and refer changing moles; a personal or family history of melanoma makes it an absolute no in the endocrinology guide. This course gives no doses or sourcing advice.

suggestedPrompt.en: What are the risks of a tanning injection such as Melanotan II?

answer.en: PTD-DBM releases a brake (CXXC5) on Wnt signalling; its whole evidence is one 2017 mouse and tissue study from the developer's group, with no human trial published or registered as of September 2026 (grade D). Zinc thymulin is a zinc-dependent thymic peptide with no indexed human hair study (grade D). In the US, on FDA's 14 May 2026 lists, thymulin acetate is in 503A Category 3 and PTD-DBM is on no list; neither is on the bulks list. Hair loss starts with a workup (pattern, trigger, patches, androgens; ferritin and TSH in everyone), and the approved options, minoxidil, finasteride in men and baricitinib for severe alopecia areata, carry grade A evidence. In the UK, a men's minoxidil foam is on general sale, finasteride for hair loss is a private prescription carrying MHRA's strengthened warnings on depression and sexual dysfunction (May 2026), baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia areata, and a peptide spray made up for one patient would be an unlicensed special that MHRA guidance places behind any licensed product that could meet the need. This course gives no doses or sourcing advice; treatment choices belong with the prescriber.
